newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Courtaulds cuts viscose capacity.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Courtaulds cuts viscose capacity.

text.p: Chemicals group Courtaulds Plc on Wednesday said it would trim its European viscose production capacity by 20 percent to fight continuing poor trading conditions, while business in its other sectors improved.
Courtaulds, whose European viscose operations are located in Britain and Germany, will reduce capacity at its Grimsby plant in northern England by 25,000 tonnes per year from 55,000.

Some 90 jobs will go, but no compulsary redundancies are expected. Courtaulds Plc said margins in the viscose business have just begun to pick up, but it expects any benefits only to come through by April.
Chief executive Gordon Campbell told Reuters the margin increase follows a price rise of about five percent.
"But it won't really work through until the next quarter," said Campbell, adding that price negotiations with customers were responsible for the delay.
Some industry analysts welcomed the capacity cut, regarding it as a sign Courtaulds was taking firm measures to address persistent oversupply in viscose markets.
But others trimmed full-year profit forecasts as Courtaulds said adverse currency movements were notably holding back improvements in the fibres and chemicals business.
A weak yen compared to the dollar hurt exports of the promising Tencel fibre from the U.S. to Japan, Courtaulds said, adding overall demand for Tencel remained strong.
Analyst Jeremy Chantry at Kleinwort Benson said he trimmed his pre-tax profit estimate for the current financial year to 134 million pounds ($219.3 million) from 140 million pounds.
Tencel is a relatively new man-made fibre derived from woodpulp. Courtaulds is the only firm to sell Tencel and has aimed supplies at the upper end of the textiles market.

Campbell said overall group pre-tax and operating profit for the year to March 31 would show an improvement when taking into account a loss of 15 million pounds in operating result due to disposals of non-core assets.
Courtaulds posted a 131.5 million pound pre-tax profit in the 1995/96 financial year.
"With the exception of viscose fibres, trading in each of our businesses has improved, despite the sluggishness of the continental European economies," Campbell said.
Courtaulds shares rose two pence to 378-1/2 pence. ($1=.6109 Pound)
